name: Watchdog Planner
blurb: a safe watchdog period and feed points from the longest task
intro: Finds the watchdog timeout that never fires in normal operation yet resets a hung system quickly: the worst gap between two feeds (normal feed interval + longest task + interrupt load) times a safety margin, checked at the fastest and slowest watchdog clock. It then picks the prescaler and reload for the chosen watchdog and lists where to feed.

inputs.label: Normal feed interval
inputs.help: How often the main loop or supervisor feeds when nothing is slow (the loop or tick period).

inputs.label: Longest task (WCET)
inputs.help: Worst-case execution time of the slowest task that runs between two feeds.

inputs.label: Interrupt load in one gap
inputs.help: Worst-case time interrupts steal during that gap.

inputs.label: Longest blocking operation
inputs.help: A one-off block such as a flash sector erase or a modem wait; 0 when there is none.

inputs.label: Watchdog clock tolerance
inputs.help: STM32 LSI is poor: F4 datasheets give 17–47 kHz (use 50 % unless calibrated); AVR ±10 %; nRF52 LFXO ±0.01 %.

inputs.label: Longest allowed hang
inputs.help: The latest a hung system may be reset (the timeout at the slowest clock must stay under it).

inputs.label: Window watchdog (feeding too early also resets)
Shortest feed gap
inputs.help: The quickest two feeds can follow each other.

examples.title: STM32 superloop: 10 ms tick, 35 ms slowest task, 400 ms flash erase
ATmega sensor node, 250 ms loop, 1 s allowed hang

usage: Give times in ms: the normal feed interval, the longest task's WCET, the interrupt load within one gap, the longest one-off blocking operation, a safety margin factor, the watchdog clock tolerance in ± percent and the longest hang you can accept; pick target stm32-iwdg, avr, nrf52 or custom (clock Hz, counter bits, largest prescaler exponent). Returns the worst feed gap, the minimum timeout, the chosen prescaler and reload, the timeout at nominal/fast/slow clock, how many extra feeds a long operation needs, and a feed-point plan. Use it when choosing or reviewing a watchdog configuration.
sources: ST RM0090 section 21 (IWDG: timeout = 4·2^PR·(RLR+1)/f_LSI) and STM32F4 datasheet LSI 17–47 kHz
Microchip ATmega328P datasheet section 10.9 (WDT prescaler, 128 kHz oscillator)
Nordic nRF52840 product specification, WDT (timeout = (CRV+1)/32768 s)
Jack Ganssle, 'Great Watchdog Timers for Embedded Systems' (feed only after all tasks check in)
